source.title: Improving scalability of parallel CNN training by adaptively adjusting parameter update frequency
source.authors: Sun-Woo Lee; Qiao Kang; Reda Al-Bahrani; Ankit Agrawal; Alok N. Choudhary; W. Liao

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a different training adaptation can preserve validation accuracy in a large-batch setting; it does not compare large batches with small batches.
record.gate_note: The paper focuses on communication cost and scalability. Its large-batch experiment reports validation accuracy for ResNet50 with and without lazy parameter updates. Results cited from earlier large-batch studies are not recorded as this paper's findings.
record.test_reason: The record overlooks the study's own batch-256 ImageNet results in Section 4.2. Across the 90-epoch experiments, ResNet50 validation accuracy falls from 75.89 ± 0.2% at batch 256 to 75.41 ± 0.1% at batch 8,192 without lazy updates. This bears on V5 using the same training method and accuracy measure, although the authors emphasize communication scalability rather than a controlled batch-size comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate as an account of the authors' conclusions. They report improved scalability with small accuracy changes and suggest that layer-dependent update frequencies could exceed a batch-size threshold. That suggestion rests on accumulating gradients from 40K–48K examples at selected layers, rather than demonstrating that an equivalent global batch preserves small-batch accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adaptive, layer-wise lazy parameter updates to reduce communication; does not measure the large-batch versus small-batch generalization gap directly.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of layers receiving lazy updates changes validation accuracy: on ImageNet, b=12, 25, and 37 yield 75.86 ± 0.1%, 75.81 ± 0.2%, and 75.33 ± 0.2%, respectively. These results are discussed as an analysis of the lazy-update method, not as a direct large-versus-small batch comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch 8,192, lazy updates reduce communication costs while preserving approximately the baseline accuracy: 75.22% versus 75.41%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing update frequency at selected input-side layers can improve distributed training scalability with a small accuracy cost.

record.problems: The large-batch accuracy comparison reports one large batch size and no small-batch reference, so it cannot establish the size of a large-batch generalization penalty. The paper states that its theoretical analysis focuses only on training loss and that lazy updates can cause a minor validation-accuracy drop.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported accuracy results are left out as rows for V5: CIFAR-10 and standard-batch ImageNet results are not large-batch comparisons. Figure 10's b=12, 25, and 37 results are separately summarized in method_sensitivity; they vary the number of lazy-update layers, not batch size.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning.

A batch-size sweep locating the workload-dependent threshold; an unadapted large-batch recipe; longer training; and controlled comparisons of normalization, regularization, or alternative scaling recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The smaller-batch results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as undeclared missing results. Their exclusion nevertheless obscures evidence relevant to V5. The fixed-batch lazy-update comparison alone would be a method-performance result, not a test of the large-batch penalty.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

The study does not compare large-batch training against small-batch training at a fixed epoch budget, nor test longer training, normalization changes, or the other named large-batch recipes. It tests lazy parameter updates with one large batch size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Train ImageNet with batch size 8,192 and linear learning-rate scaling, without lazy parameter updates.

conditions.value: initial 3.2; decays by factor of 10 after 30, 60, and 80 epochs; warm-up in first 5 epochs

rows.note: Reference value for the lazy-update comparison; no small-batch result is reported here.
rows.check: The value is correct, but the claim that no small-batch reference is reported overlooks Section 4.2 and Figure 6: batch 256 achieves 75.89 ± 0.2% over 90 epochs. Against that reference, accuracy is 0.48 percentage points lower. Learning rate and warmup adapt with batch size; statistical significance is not reported.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Train ImageNet with batch size 8,192 and linear learning-rate scaling, using lazy parameter updates at the bottom 24 layers.

conditions.value: with; 24 bottom layers; average update interval between 5 and 6
initial 3.2; decays by factor of 10 after 30, 60, and 80 epochs; warm-up in first 5 epochs

rows.note: The authors describe the result as comparable to the baseline; the paper does not provide a small-batch comparison.
rows.check: The recorded baseline measures the lazy-update intervention at fixed batch size, which alone cannot establish V5. Section 4.2 supplies a smaller-batch lazy-update reference of 75.81 ± 0.2%, versus 75.22 ± 0.1% here. The 0.59-point difference is descriptive: the number of lazy-update layers also changes from 25 to 24.

relationships.condition: ResNet50 on ImageNet, 90 epochs, batch 256 versus 8,192, without lazy updates and with learning-rate adaptation
relationships.reason: R1 reaches 75.41 ± 0.1%, versus the text's smaller-batch 75.89 ± 0.2%; this supports a modest residual large-batch penalty across these experiments.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest the larger batch retained a modest accuracy deficit despite learning-rate adaptation. These results have not been verified.

relationships.condition: ResNet50 on ImageNet, 90 epochs, with lazy updates and learning-rate adaptation
relationships.reason: R2 reaches 75.22 ± 0.1%, versus the text's batch-256 result of 75.81 ± 0.2%; the descriptive penalty remains, although lazy-update layer counts also differ.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest a residual accuracy deficit with lazy updates, although the number of affected layers also differed. These results have not been verified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet50 on ImageNet with batch size 8,192, 90 epochs, and lazy updates at the bottom 24 layers
reader_labels.reason: Validation accuracy is reported as comparable to the no-lazy-update baseline (R1–R2); this supports preservation under the tested adaptation, not removal of a measured small-batch penalty.
